questions.question: What is the main purpose of a marine diesel engine?
options: To propel the vessel or generate electrical power
questions.explanation: Marine diesel engines are mainly used for propulsion or for driving generators that produce electrical power.

questions.question: Which fuel is commonly used in large marine diesel engines?
options: Heavy fuel oil or marine diesel oil
questions.explanation: Large marine engines commonly operate on heavy fuel oil, marine diesel oil or other approved marine fuels.

questions.question: What happens inside the cylinder during combustion?
options: Fuel burns and produces expanding gases that push the piston
Cooling water pushes the piston downward
Lubricating oil is converted into fuel
Exhaust gas is stored in the cylinder
questions.explanation: The injected fuel ignites in the hot compressed air, creating high-pressure gases that force the piston downward.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the fuel injection system?
options: To deliver the correct quantity of fuel at the correct time
To pump seawater through the engine
questions.explanation: The injection system meters, pressurizes and injects fuel into the cylinder at the correct point in the engine cycle.

questions.question: Why is lubricating oil used in a marine diesel engine?
options: To reduce friction and wear between moving components
questions.explanation: Lubricating oil reduces friction, limits wear, removes some heat and helps protect engine components from corrosion.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the engine cooling system?
options: To remove excess heat and maintain safe operating temperatures
questions.explanation: The cooling system transfers heat away from components such as cylinder liners, cylinder heads and pistons.

questions.question: In a four-stroke diesel engine, how many crankshaft revolutions are required to complete one operating cycle?
questions.explanation: A four-stroke cycle consists of intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes and requires two crankshaft revolutions.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a two-stroke and a four-stroke marine diesel engine?
options: A two-stroke engine completes a cycle in one crankshaft revolution
A two-stroke engine does not require fuel
A four-stroke engine has no exhaust system
A four-stroke engine cannot drive a generator
questions.explanation: A two-stroke engine completes one full operating cycle during one crankshaft revolution, while a four-stroke engine requires two.

questions.question: What is scavenging in a two-stroke marine diesel engine?
options: Removing exhaust gases and supplying fresh air to the cylinder
questions.explanation: Scavenging replaces exhaust gases in the cylinder with fresh pressurized air before the next combustion cycle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a turbocharger on a marine diesel engine?
options: To use exhaust energy to compress more intake air into the engine
To reduce the crankshaft speed to zero
questions.explanation: The turbocharger uses exhaust-gas energy to drive a compressor, increasing the mass of air supplied to the cylinders.

questions.question: Why must heavy fuel oil normally be heated before injection?
options: To reduce its viscosity and improve atomization
To prevent compression in the cylinder
To reduce the amount of intake air
questions.explanation: Heavy fuel oil is heated so that it reaches the correct viscosity for pumping, injection and fine atomization.

questions.question: What may happen if a fuel injector does not atomize the fuel correctly?
options: Poor combustion, increased smoke and carbon deposits
Lower cylinder pressure with perfect combustion
The cooling system stops using water
questions.explanation: Poor atomization produces larger fuel droplets, resulting in incomplete combustion, smoke, deposits and reduced efficiency.
